name: Canva
h1_tail: Funding Rounds, Share Prices and Ownership
description: Canva is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors, funds and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Canva is a privately held design software company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $200 million round announced on September 14, 2021, valued the company at $40 billion.

Based in Sydney, Canva operates an online design platform, launched in 2013, that individuals and organizations use to create presentations, documents, social media graphics, videos and other visual materials. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Canva
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round.
round_notes: In August 2025, Canva said that current and former employees would sell shares to investors led by Fidelity in a transaction that valued the company at $42 billion; an employee share sale in October 2024 had valued it at $32 billion. In February 2026, Canva said its annual recurring revenue had reached $4 billion at the end of 2025; that figure is the company's own.

A round price reflects what investors paid for the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: T. Rowe Price led the September 2021 round, joined by Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer Venture Partners, Greenoaks Capital, Dragoneer Investments, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree Ventures. Dragoneer co-led the April 2021 round, and Blackbird and Sequoia Capital China co-led the June 2020 round. Other investors include Bond, General Catalyst, Skip Capital, Fidelity and J.P. Morgan Asset Management.
spv_sentence: Since 2024, five special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Canva have filed with the SEC, none of them in 2026.
funds: Mutual funds and other SEC-registered funds managed by Fidelity and J.P. Morgan, among others, reported Canva holdings in filings for periods in 2026. Fundrise Growth Tech Fund valued its position at $9.6 million as of June 30, 2026.
sources: Sources: reports by TechCrunch (September 2021, June 2020, October 2019, February 2026 and August 2013), Fortune (April 2021 and August 2025) and Reuters (August 2025); and SEC Form D and Form N-PORT filings.
